ctx.x: You see? Did you ever go to the Tantai Social Club? The who?
Tanty Social Club. Oh, uh, no, I never did. That's, Sharky played there.
Yeah, but you didn't go there.

items.title: Sharkey Bonano Interview, 1966-11-09
items.q: Harry James. He had the trombone player. He was in the Army and got lost in the plane. Glenn Miller he had. Ray Badu. Eddie Miller. Snappy Lamar. He had all of them.

ctx.x: Is Harry James one of those names?
Harry James. He had the trombone player. He was in the Army and got lost in the plane. Glenn Miller he had. Ray Badu. Eddie Miller. Snappy Lamar. He had all of them.
Oh yeah, that old band he had with Benny Goodman and other.

items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-26
items.q: Well, Sharky, I don't wanna mess you up. But... You better keep him because I don't know if any other drummer on here.

ctx.x: How did Monk Hazel rate in those days? He played good drums.

Monk was a good drum. I don't know whether he was a great reader or not, but like I say... No. I mean... He played with my brother Jules for quite a while. Yeah. In different bands around the world. He played... Then later on he went with... He went with Sharky, see. And when I left Jimmy Darcy in 51, I came down there. Sharky said, man... He said, the guy driving in... He gets knocked out of his skull and he can't play. Yeah. I said, well... Well, Sharky, I don't wanna mess you up. But... You better keep him…
Yeah, well... It'll turn up. I can come back tomorrow... And look at him some more. You have time tomorrow? I... It's alright with me, but I'm saying...
